rows.selection_reason: With no prior evidence, the priority is to establish a clean multimodal baseline that is cheap and interpretable. config_001 (multimodal, singleprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, concat) is the simplest full multimodal configuration: PCA is nearly free, ResNet50 is a moderate-cost CNN, singleprofile avoids aggregation overhead, and concat is trivial. This experiment tests whether a straightforward multimodal fusion of standard features achieves a competitive accuracy, giving us a floor to compare against more expensive encoders (scgpt, ViT-L), multiprofile aggregation, and alternative fusion strategies in subsequent runs. It is the best use of experiment 1 because it is low-cost (expected relative cost: low, roughly 1× a baseline run), preserves GPU budget for the 9 remaining experiments, and immediately tells us whether the multimodal signal is strong enough to justify investing in heavier encoders and aggregation in later trials.

Evidence: config_001 (multimodal, singleprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, concat) achieved only 52.7% validation accuracy at 0.85 GPU hours. With just one data point, the most critical uncertainty is whether the image modality is actually contributing signal or adding noise. Question tested: config_045 (rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) is a clean A/B comparison that removes only the image branch while keeping the RNA encoder, profile setting, and architecture identical to config_001. If RNA-alone matches or exceeds 52.7%, the image modality is not helping and I should redirect remaining budget toward RNA encoder upgrades (scgpt, scvi_n200) and multiprofile aggregation. If RNA-alone is substantially lower, multimodal fusion is confirmed valuable and I should prioritize image encoder (ViT-L) and fusion strategy improvements. Why this is the best next experiment: it is extremely cheap (~0.3–0.5 GPU hours, RNA-only with PCA and no image processing), so it costs a small fraction of the budget while resolving the single most consequential design question—whether to invest remaining experiments in multimodal or unimodal architectures. This information will shape the strategy for all 8 remaining experiments far more effectively than a small incremental change (e.g., switching concat→weighted fusion) or a costly multimodal variant that conflates multiple variables.

Evidence: config_001 (multimodal, singleprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, concat) achieved 0.527 acc, clearly outperforming the RNA-only baseline (0.485 acc), confirming that image information adds value. However, all tested configs use singleprofile; the multiprofile dimension is completely untested and represents a major architectural change that could significantly improve performance by aggregating information across multiple profiles. Question: Does multiprofile with avgpool aggregation improve over singleprofile when keeping the same encoders (pca_n2000, resnet50) and fusion (concat)? This isolates the multiprofile+aggregation effect cleanly. Rationale: With 7 experiments remaining, resolving whether multiprofile helps is the highest-value uncertainty to reduce—if it does, it opens a large family of multiprofile variants (scgpt, ViT-L, transformer aggregation) to exploit; if it doesn't, we avoid wasting budget on expensive multiprofile configs. config_038 uses avgpool (cheaper than transformer) and keeps the same encoders/fusion as config_001, making it a controlled comparison. Expected cost: ~1.3–1.6 GPU hours (moderately higher than config_001's 0.85 due to multiprofile processing and avgpool aggregation, but well below transformer-based variants).

Evidence: config_038 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, concat) achieved the best accuracy so far (0.6186), a large jump over the singleprofile baseline (0.5266). The multiprofile + avgpool + concat + resnet50 pipeline is validated as strong. The weakest component in that pipeline is the RNA encoder: pca_n2000 is a linear dimensionality reduction that may discard nonlinear biological signal. Question: Does upgrading the RNA encoder to scgpt (a pretrained transformer capturing gene-expression semantics) while holding all other components fixed improve validation accuracy beyond 0.6186? This is the single most impactful untested change on the current best configuration. Why this is the best use of experiment 4: it directly exploits the strongest evidence (config_038) with a one-variable extension, reducing uncertainty about whether a richer RNA representation can push accuracy higher. Expected relative cost: scgpt is a transformer-based encoder applied per-cell across multiple profiles, so this will be moderately more expensive than config_038's 36.42 GPU-hr run—estimated ~45–55 GPU hours—making it the most expensive option among the single-change extensions, but justified because it targets the component most likely to yield a meaningful accuracy gain.

Evidence: config_038 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, concat) is the clear best at 0.619 acc, showing that multiprofile+avgpool aggregation and PCA-2000 are the key winning factors. The image modality contributes meaningfully (config_001 multimodal 0.527 vs config_045 RNA-only 0.485), but ResNet50 may be a bottleneck for image representation quality. Question: Does upgrading the image encoder from ResNet50 to ImageNet ViT-L (a substantially stronger pretrained visual backbone) improve on the 0.619 baseline while keeping all other settings identical? This is a single-variable change from the best config, isolating the image encoder's contribution. Why this is the best next experiment: With 5 experiments remaining, the highest-leverage untested axis is the image encoder strength. A stronger visual representation is the most plausible path to a meaningful accuracy gain over 0.619. Expected relative cost: ViT-L is larger than ResNet50, so this will be more expensive than config_038's 36.42 GPU hours—estimated ~45-55 GPU hours. This is a significant cost, but justified because it directly targets the most likely improvement over the current best, and a failure here would still leave 4 experiments to explore weighted fusion or transformer aggregation variants.

The evidence strongly points to multiprofile + pca_n2000 + imagenet_vit_l as the optimal backbone: config_049 (avgpool, concat) achieved 0.629 acc at only 4.54 GPU hrs, beating config_038 (resnet50, 36.42 GPU hrs) and config_021 (scgpt, 0.512 acc). The remaining uncertainty is whether weighted fusion can improve over simple concat at the same aggregation level. config_009 isolates exactly this one variable (concat → weighted) while keeping all other hyperparameters at their proven-best values. It is expected to cost roughly the same as config_049 (~4.5 GPU hrs), making it a cheap, high-information experiment. If weighted fusion yields a meaningful gain, subsequent experiments can layer on transformer aggregation; if not, we can pivot to testing transformer aggregation (config_022/037) with the remaining budget. This is the best use of experiment 6 because it reduces uncertainty on the last untested dimension of the current best configuration at minimal cost.

The current best (config_009, acc=0.6352) uses pca_n2000 + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + weighted. The only untested dimension for this top-performing combination is aggregation type: all top configs use avgpool, but transformer aggregation has never been paired with this exact set of encoders and weighted fusion. config_037 (pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) isolates that single change. Evidence strongly favors pca_n2000 over scgpt (0.61–0.64 vs 0.51) and imagenet_vit_l over resnet50 (0.63 vs 0.62), so exploring a different aggregation on this proven backbone is the highest-information next step. If transformer aggregation captures cross-profile interactions better than simple averaging, it could push accuracy above 0.635; if not, it confirms avgpool is optimal and the remaining 3 experiments can target other levers. Expected cost: moderate—transformer aggregation adds self-attention over profiles on top of the ViT-L backbone, so I estimate roughly 10–15 GPU hours (about 1.5–2× config_009's 7.02 hrs), which is well within the remaining budget of ~47 GPU hours.

The current best is config_009 (pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted, multiprofile) at 0.635 accuracy. The architecture components—multiprofile, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion—are well-supported by the evidence (avgpool > transformer by ~5 pts; weighted ≥ concat; multiprofile >> singleprofile; imagenet_vit_l > resnet50 at similar cost). The main untested variable that could push accuracy higher is the RNA encoder: scgpt was clearly worse (0.512), but scvi_n200 (a learned variational encoder) has not been paired with the best image/fusion stack. config_032 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted, multiprofile) directly tests whether a learned RNA representation can outperform PCA while keeping all other parameters at their proven-optimal settings. This is a focused exploitation of the strongest configuration with one targeted change. Expected cost is moderate (~5–8 GPU hours), comparable to config_009 (7.02 h) since scvi_n200 is a learned encoder similar in complexity to scgpt (4.33 h in config_021), keeping total budget well within limits for the remaining 2 experiments.

The current best is config_032 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + multiprofile + avgpool + weighted) at 0.706 accuracy. The strongest evidence shows scvi_n200 is the dominant RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l the best image encoder, and multiprofile > singleprofile. The one remaining uncertainty is aggregation: transformer underperformed avgpool with pca_n2000 (config_037: 0.586 vs config_009: 0.635), but scvi_n200 produces a richer learned representation that may benefit more from attention-based aggregation than a static PCA projection. config_019 (scvi_n200 + vit_l + transformer + weighted) directly tests this hypothesis while keeping the proven weighted fusion. This is the only untested configuration with a realistic chance of exceeding 0.706, since all other untested scvi_n200+vit_l variants either use concat (weaker evidence) or singleprofile (weaker evidence). Expected cost is moderate (~5–7 GPU hours), comparable to config_037 (4.55) and config_032 (4.82), since scvi_n200 is a compact encoder and the transformer aggregation adds only modest overhead over avgpool.

The current best is config_019 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted, acc=0.725). The evidence strongly supports scvi_n200 as the best RNA encoder (~8% gain over pca_n2000), imagenet_vit_l as the best image encoder, transformer aggregation over avgpool (~2% gain), and weighted fusion over concat (~1-2% gain). The only untested variant within this top-performing design space is config_046 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + concat). While weighted fusion has consistently outperformed concat in prior comparisons, this is the last experiment and config_046 is the closest untested neighbor to the best configuration, offering a small chance of competitive performance while confirming the fusion-choice conclusion. All other untested configs involve a known inferior component (scgpt, resnet50, singleprofile, rna_only) and are very unlikely to beat 0.725. Expected relative cost: moderate (~3.5–4.5 GPU hours), comparable to config_019 and config_037, making it a low-risk final experiment that does not add disproportionate cost to the 66.18 GPU hours already spent.
